gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the DXP4800 Plus's Pentium Gold 8505 scores 3,197 in PassMark single-thread. That is 2.8× the Synology DS925+'s Ryzen V1500B (1,136) and 2.1× the QNAP TS-464's Celeron N5095 (1,492), and single-thread speed is the figure Minecraft's tick loop depends on.
standout_why: racksandwatts.com and esp32.co.uk, the two cited rivals, list each model's CPU name and RAM only. Neither gives a benchmark score, a price, a power figure or any mention of Minecraft. The ugreen.com pages ChatGPT cited are the maker's own DXP4800 Plus pages and have no cross-brand comparison. ChatGPT's answer says 'Minecraft Java Edition relies heavily on single-core CPU performance' but gives no number for any candidate.
decides: It confirms the DXP4800 Plus as the pick and pushes the Synology DS925+ down. The DS925+ costs about as much as the DXP4800 Plus, but its CPU has the lowest single-thread score of the four, below even the cheaper DXP2800's N100 (1,879 vs 1,136, 1.65×). The QNAP TS-464 also falls behind the $389.99 DXP2800 on this measure. Per dollar the two UGREENs are close: the DXP4800 Plus gives 5.2 single-thread points per dollar and the DXP2800 gives 4.8. So the DXP4800 Plus wins on raw tick speed without costing more per point.

unsourced: UGREEN's own power figures for the DXP2800 and DXP4800 Plus: nas.ugreen.com and ai.ugreen.com returned HTTP 429 to every fetch. it-connect.fr lists 42.36 W in use and 18.12 W standby for the DXP4800 Plus, but doesn't say whether it measured them or copied the spec, so I left them out. Igor's Lab and Neowin, which measured the DXP2800, both returned 403. That means there is no kWh-per-year figure for either UGREEN to set against QNAP and Synology.
